name: The Deep-Forging
summary: The moment the deep-folk became a people: Orbren's hammer fell on the Stone Crown, and where it struck, the first halls were opened. Before the Deep-Forging the deep-folk were cave-dwellers and surface herders; after it they were a civilization of signed steel, spoken law, and doors. Every hold, every oath-ring, and every sealed door on Aurelith descends from the strikes made in that generation.

participants.name: orbren
participants.note: walked among mortals openly — this was before the Withdrawal; his hammer-fall is remembered as sound, not metaphor

participants.name: deep-folk
participants.note: nine tribes under the Stone Crown received the hammer in turn

course_of_events.what: The nine tribes send nine speakers into the mountain's root to ask the earth for shelter from the long winters above. The saga says the earth answered with a knock.

Orbren strikes the Stone Crown; the first hall opens 'like an eye'. He teaches for a generation: the hammer, the forge, the oath-ring, and the rule that every opening must be earned and every closing must be kept.
Hallord's heart-fire is lit from Orbren's own forge-heat. It has never gone out. The first laws are sworn here because nothing written can be trusted yet — only memory and fire.
The holds spread through the Crown's root. The first Door-Keepers are sworn when a gallery opens onto something that should have stayed shut. Khord's silence enters the law.

key_places.name: The Hammerfall Gallery
key_places.description: The first opened hall, deepest of all Hallord's works. Its walls bear a single dent the size of a god's fist. Pilgrims touch it once per lifetime.

key_places.name: The First Forge
key_places.description: Hallord's heart: lit ~415 AS, never extinguished. All deep-folk law is sworn here; all signed steel is trusted because of it.

key_places.name: The Nine Speakers' Seats
key_places.description: Nine stone seats at the mountain's root where the tribes first asked the earth for shelter. Vacant by custom — no one sits in a god's audience.

consequences: Deep-folk civilization begins: craft, spoken law, oath-rings, and the doctrine of closed doors.
Orbren becomes the one deity every species later names the same — the forge-god's teaching outlived the gods' presence.
The Sunken Halls' architecture of 'earned openings' shapes deep-folk culture to this day.
remembrance: Forging-Day is the deep-folk year's highest feast: fires are re-struck symbolically, apprentices take their first hammer-stroke, and the saga of the Nine Speakers is spoken aloud in every hold simultaneously.
adventure_hooks: A surface scholar claims the Hammerfall dent is natural geology; Hallord offers players the chance to prove otherwise — or be proven wrong forever.
An apprentice steals a hammer-stroke on Forging-Day (unheard of); the scandal reaches the Ring-Vault.
Something knocks back from beyond the Lowest Door — three times, like the earth answering.
